newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL -- IBM resumes ascent.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL -- IBM resumes ascent.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp shares traded higher preceding Thursday's market open, reversing a selloff that occured in the last hour of trade yesterday.
Early today, IBM rose to 153-5/8 from 152-3/4, restarting a sharp climb that began November 14 from about 135 per share.
In late NYSE trade Wednesday, IBM fell to 152-3/4 -- closing off 1-1/2 -- from an intraday high 159, leading a group of large capitalization tech stocks off their peaks.
Traders also said a false rumor of a downgrade of IBM by SoundView Financial contributed to yesterday's fall.
Guidant Corp strengthened early Thursday on buying related to the stock's addition to the Standard & Poor's 500 index, traders said.
Guidant rose to 53 from 50-1/4 preceding the market open.
Sunglass Hut International Inc fell to 6-1/4 from 7-3/8, breaking down to a new year-low after reporting a third fiscal quarter loss of $0.05 per share compared to a profit of $0.05 one year ago.
The results were well short of the Wall Street consensus estimate of $0.02 per share profit, as compiled by Zack's Investment Research.
Conrail Inc fell to 94-1/2 from 96-7/8 as CSX Corp commenced its tender offer for the company at $110 per share.
The offer is the first step of two-step transaction. The second step is a stock swap.

The offer effectively begins the takeover of Conrail by CSX, a deal that competes with a higher Conrail bid from Norfolk Southern, which unsuccessfully tried to block the CSX deal in U.S. District Court in Philadelphia Tuesday.
CompuServe Corp fell to 11 from 11-5/8 after the company reported a loss of $0.63 per share, or $58 million in the fiscal second quarter.
